newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to cremate late leader at state funeral.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to cremate late leader at state funeral.

text.p: Former Sri Lankan president Junius Richard Jayewardene, who died on Friday at age 90, will be cremated with full state honours, his United National Party (UNP) said on Saturday.

The funeral will be on Monday at Kelaniya, a northern suburb of Colombo, despite a government offer to hold it at Independence Square closer to the heart of the city, UNP's general secretary Gamini Athukorala told Reuters.
"The late president's family wanted it held at Kelaniya in accordance with his wish," Athukorala said.
Jayewardene, who ruled the Indian Ocean island from 1977 to 1988 as prime minister and as its first executive president, died in a private hospital after a brief illness.
His body would lie in state at his home in Colombo's fashionable Ward Place area until the cremation, the UNP said.
The village of Kelaniya, on the banks of the Kelani river, is Jayewardene's home seat that he successfully contested to enter parliament in 1943.
Athukorala said the cremation would take place near a historic Buddhist temple at Kelaniya. His ashes would be scattered over the river, he added.
The government of President Chandrika Kumaratunga has requested the national flag to be flown at half staff to honour the late leader, the Department of Information said.

Jayawardene's reputation as a strongman and one of South Asia's shrewdest leaders suffered after his mid-1980s efforts to settle Sri Lanka's ethnic conflict failed and Tamil rebels intensified their war, which still plagues the country.
After his retirement in 1989 from 50 years of political life, Jayewardene bore the brunt of criticism for the island's economic and political ills.
